html:
A poet and playwright from Saint Lucia in the eastern Caribbean, whose work explored the history, landscapes and mixed identity of the Caribbean. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1992.

He grew up in Castries, of African and European descent, with English as his school language and French Creole all around him. He published his first poems at 18. He spent many years in Trinidad, where he founded the Trinidad Theatre Workshop, and later taught in the United States.

His poems ask what it means to be heir to both the slave trade and to the language and books of the empire that ran it. His best known work is Omeros (1990), a long poem that retells Homer's story in the lives of Saint Lucian fishermen, giving them the dignity of the Homeric heroes. His play Dream on Monkey Mountain (1967) is also widely known. He showed that the islands' history could be the stuff of epic.
sum: A poet and playwright from Saint Lucia in the eastern Caribbean, whose work explored the history, landscapes and mixed identity of the Caribbean. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1992.
